title: Excel for financial modelling
why: Almost every valuation, budget and investment decision is first built in a spreadsheet model. A clear, auditable model is how finance people earn trust.
what_is_different: Financial modellers live in the keyboard, build three linked statements, separate inputs from calculations, and obsess over checks and sign conventions. Charts matter less than integrity, flexibility and speed.

extra_modules.title: Keyboard-first working
extra_modules.outcome: You can: navigate and build without the mouse
topics: shortcuts for navigation, selection, fill and formatting
consistent colour coding (inputs blue, formulas black)
extra_modules.practice: Rebuild a small table using only the keyboard

extra_modules.title: Three-statement model
extra_modules.outcome: You can: link income statement, balance sheet and cash flow
extra_modules.practice: Build a five-year three-statement model for a simple business

extra_modules.title: Time-series and timing flags
extra_modules.outcome: You can: model monthly, quarterly and annual periods correctly
extra_modules.practice: Add a construction period and an operating period flag

extra_modules.title: Valuation
extra_modules.outcome: You can: value a business or project
extra_modules.practice: Value the model's business with a DCF and sensitivity table

extra_modules.title: Scenarios and model review
extra_modules.outcome: You can: stress-test and review a model like an auditor
extra_modules.practice: Add base/upside/downside scenarios and review another person's model

starter_project: Build a three-statement model and DCF for a small business (for example, a bakery or a solar mini-grid) with three scenarios and a one-page dashboard.
pitfalls: Mixing inputs and calculations on the same sheet
Sign errors between cash flow and balance sheet
Circular references hidden with iterative calculation

expert_validation.note: AI-drafted outline; to be validated by a practitioner and an educator in this field.
